errors.english: [note: This indicates the patience of subsequent realization regarding cessation.]
errors.why: The identification of Subhūti's reply with the subsequent-knowledge forbearance regarding cessation (nirodhe 'nvayajñānakṣānti) is the commentator's own statement in the text, not a translator's note.

fix.find: [note: This indicates the patience of subsequent realization regarding cessation.]
fix.replace: These words are the forbearance of subsequent knowledge with regard to cessation.

note: A faithful rendering of the repetitive sūtra questions; the commentary's own gloss is demoted to a bracketed translator's note, and the opening adds a stray gloss about Subhūti.

errors.english: is not the defining characteristic of the meditative absorption of yoga
errors.why: The Tibetan says the samādhi of single recollection IS the characteristic of the yoga samādhi that is a limb of the first application; there is no negation.

fix.find: is not the defining characteristic of the meditative absorption of yoga
fix.replace: is the defining characteristic of the meditative absorption of yoga

note: Otherwise an accurate account of the sādhana sequence, but an added negation reverses the opening definition.

errors.english: This is found in many (sutras) discourses endowed with the (paramitas) perfections and should be viewed in the systems of (mantra) secret formula; tantra as well.
errors.why: The Tibetan begins a new clause about the commentator looking at many Pāramitā sūtras and mantra systems (continuing on the next side), not a claim that the quotation is found in them and should be viewed in tantra.

note: The ten-entries passage is rendered faithfully; only the final transitional clause is recast.

errors.english: Action refers to what has been transformed.
errors.why: ལས here is the ablative 'from' of the lemma ཧཱུཾ་དེར་གྱུར་པ་ལས ('from that HŪṂ transformed') begun on the previous side, not 'action' (karman).

errors.english: This signifies a perfect teaching arising from great compassion and attachment.
errors.why: The phrase means the (reddish) colour shows that he is attached through great compassion; སྟོན་པ is 'showing', not 'a perfect teaching'.

note: Sound on the iconography and the third-yoga procedure, with two lemma glosses misread.

errors.english: because the blue color [note: original: "sngon", often used as a standard example for sensory perception] has already appeared. When the nature of the blue itself appears, other aspects are precisely what are not clear.
errors.why: སྔོན here is 'earlier/before' (it appeared previously; when it appears in its earlier nature the other aspect is unclear), not 'blue' (སྔོན་པོ).

fix.find: because the blue color [note: original: "sngon", often used as a standard example for sensory perception] has already appeared. When the nature of the blue itself appears, other aspects are precisely what are not clear.
fix.replace: because it already appeared earlier. When it appears in its earlier nature, the other aspect is precisely what is not clear.

errors.english: [note: original: "khra bo", referring to a multicolored or complex pattern]
errors.why: ཁྲ་བོ is the 'dappled one', the standard example of an individual cow (śābaleya) from the preceding argument about the cognition 'this is a cow', not a multicoloured pattern.

errors.english: If those who claim there is no conceptualization in perception argue that conceptualization is something else entirely and thus causes an interruption
errors.why: The objection is put by the opponent against the proponent of non-conceptual perception: 'for one who holds perception non-conceptual, conceptualization is something else, so it interrupts'; the proponents themselves do not argue this.

note: The dialectic is mostly followed, but a misread སྔོན ('earlier' taken as 'blue') derails one step of the argument and the cow example is lost.

errors.english: The Body, Speech, and Mind Vajra of those, which causes everyone to tremble, is the nature of the Wrathful Mantra
errors.why: The body, speech and mind vajra of 'those' (the beings to be accomplished) is what gets terrified; the terrifier is the one whose nature is the wrathful mantra.

fix.find: The Body, Speech, and Mind Vajra of those, which causes everyone to tremble, is the nature of the Wrathful Mantra
fix.replace: That which utterly terrifies the Body, Speech, and Mind Vajra of those is the one whose nature is the Wrathful Mantra

note: The coded commitments and the summary are well rendered; the terrifying clause has its object turned into the agent.
Faithful rendering of the five-similes verse, the two-truths gloss and the humoral timing of dreams.

errors.english: The Apabhraṃśa phrase ehu so para­mamahāsuhau would be eṣo 'sau parama­mahā­sukhaḥ.
errors.why: The Tibetan has no remark on an Apabhraṃśa phrase and its Sanskrit equivalent; this comes from the Sanskrit commentary, not from this side.

fix.find: The Apabhraṃśa phrase ehu so para­mamahāsuhau would be eṣo 'sau parama­mahā­sukhaḥ.

errors.english: While innate joy is cultivated through elimination.
errors.why: The Tibetan says the remaining (fourth) one is innate joy; there is nothing about cultivating it through elimination.

note: A close, scholarly translation (apparently made from the Sanskrit) that tracks the Tibetan well apart from a Sanskrit-only aside and one verse line.

errors.english: Because the parents are the masters of the body's development, if there is little love, there is little benefit.
errors.why: The Tibetan says the parents of eunuchs etc. are responsible for their deficient (incomplete) body and have little love for them, hence their benefit is small; 'deficient' is lost and the causal pair becomes a vague conditional.

note: A sound rendering of the Kośa discussion of the ānantarya acts, with the reasoning about eunuchs' parents blurred.

errors.english:
it is the destruction of existing things by denigrating the cause, the effect, or the activity. This distorted conceptualization is characterized by functions that include:
*   Engaging in patience, desire, intelligence, reflection, and vision that sever all roots of virtue.
errors.why: Wrong view is a list of alternatives (denying cause, effect or function; destroying an existing thing; wrong conceptualization), as the following explanation of each confirms, and acceptance/wish/intellect/conception/view are synonyms of the view itself, whose function is severing the roots of virtue.

fix.find:
it is the destruction of existing things by denigrating the cause, the effect, or the activity. This distorted conceptualization is characterized by functions that include:
*   Engaging in patience, desire, intelligence, reflection, and vision that sever all roots of virtue.
fix.replace:
it is the acceptance, wish, intellect, conception, and view that denigrates the cause, the effect, or the activity, or destroys an existing thing, or wrongly conceptualizes. Its functions are:
*   Severing all roots of virtue.

errors.english: This view involves a functional basis where patience, desire, intelligence, reflection, and vision result only in fruitless exhaustion.
errors.why: Acceptance, wish, intellect, conception and view are the names of the view of holding ethics and observances supreme; its function is to be the basis of fruitless exertion, not that these five result in exhaustion.

note: The examples of denigrating cause, effect and activity are rendered well, but the definitional formula is mis-segmented, merging the alternatives of wrong view.
